NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, DECEMBER 25, 1936 18091

〔此处转录不清〕

SHIPMENT OF TREASURES
COMPLETED

Nanking, Dec. 23.
The transportation of art relics of
the Peiping Palace Museum, stored in
Shanghai for the past two years, from
the port city to Nanking has now been
completed. The Shanghai Office of
the Museum, it is learned, will short-
ly be abolished.—Central News.

CHIN

珍宝运输
已完成

南京，12月23日电。
过去两年存于上海的北平故宫博物院文物，从该港口城市运往南京的工作现已完成。据悉，该院上海办事处不久将撤销。——中央通讯社。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, December 14, 1936

D. 7451
15 12 36

More Palace Treasure
Shipped To Nanking

The third shipment of art treasures of the old Peking Palace Museum was being removed today from the Ben Building, Rue Montauban, to the Markham Road Railway Junction where special coaches will transport the art relics to Nanking, starting at 10 p.m. tonight under guard.
Removal of the treasures was conducted practically in the same manner as in the two previous shipments. The premises of the godown, were heavily guarded by officers of the Settlement and the Concession. Work was to continue until about 6 p.m. today. According to an official of the Museum, some 4000 cases of art relics was expected to be removed to today,

Today's shipment is part of the 20,000 cases of the treasures which have been housed in Shanghai since early in 1933 as result of the Japanese menace in Peiping. In the first two consignments some 8000 boxes have been sent to Nanking where the relics will be put in special vaults until arrangements are completed to house the treasures in a permanent structure.

Two more shipments are scheduled, next Thursday and Monday when the removing will be conducted simultaneously in the two godowns of the Ben Buildings, one on Rue Montauban and the other at 32 Szechuen Road,

此次珍宝搬迁的方式与前两次几乎相同。仓库 premises 由租界和法租界的警官严密守卫。工作将持续至今日下午6时左右。据博物院一位官员称，预计今日将搬出约4000箱文物，

今日的运输是自从1933年初因北平日方威胁而存于上海的20,000箱珍宝的一部分。在前两批货物中，约有8000箱已运往南京，这些文物将被放入特制保险库中，直到为永久安置这些珍宝的设施安排妥当为止。

另有两批运输计划定于下周四和周一进行，届时将在本大楼的两个仓库同时开展搬迁工作，一个位于蒙塔班路，另一个位于四川路32号，

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, December 11, 1936

More Treasures Leave City Bound
For Nanking; Art Heavily Guarded

THE second shipment of art treasures of the old Peking Palace Museum, which have been stored in Shanghai since 1933, was being removed today from the Ben Building to the Markham Road Railway Junction where they will be shipped to Nanking on special coaches starting at 10 p.m. tonight. A heavy cordon of 20 Settlement Chinese constables of the Reserve Unit under the supervision of Sub-Inspector F. Hancock and Probationary-Sergeant J. S. Bushby and 20 more Chinese constables from the Special Brigade of the French Municipal Police under Brigadier L. Asdrubal guarded the premises and the transportation.

Work started shortly after 6 a.m. this morning practically in the same manner as it was conducted on Wednesday morning, and it was to continue until 6 p.m. today. A fleet of 30 Marden trucks was at work, each truck loading about 30 boxes on the average. Each truck was escorted by two Chinese constables, one each from the Settlement and the Concession, and the trucks went to the station in groups of 10. Some 5000 cases of the trea-sures are expected to be shipped to Nanking today, according to an official of the Museum.

This second consignment is a part of the 20,000 cases which have been housed in the Ben Building at Rue Montauban and 32 Szechuen Road. In the first consignment on Wednesday some 3351 boxes of the valuable treasures were shipped to Nanking. The treasures in the Rue Montauban Ben Building will be removed first and in the later installments the remaining treasures in the Szechuen Road Ben Building will be removed. The third and fourth consignments are scheduled next Monday and Thursday.

The collection of the treasures when removed to the capital will be temporarily stored in specially built vaults, built by a foreign firm, until arrangements are completed to house them in permanent quarters for public display. The collection includes the 91 odd boxes of art treasures which were exhibited from November, 1935, to March of this year, at the Burlington House, London.

更多珍宝离沪
运往南京；艺术品受严密警卫

原北平故宫博物院自1933年起存于上海的第二批艺术珍宝，今日正从本大楼搬往麦根路（Markham Road）铁路联运站，届时将于今晚10时由专用车厢启运至南京。由副督察 F. Hancock 和见习警长 J. S. Bushby  supervising 的预备队20名华捕，以及在 L. Asdrubal 巡佐指挥下的法国公董局警务处特别大队的20名华捕，组成了严密的警戒线，守卫着场所及运输过程。

工作于今晨6点后不久开始，方式与周三上午几乎相同，并将持续至今日下午6时。一支由30辆马登（Marden）卡车组成的车队正在作业，平均每辆卡车载重约30箱。每辆卡车由两名华捕护送，分别来自公共租界和法租界，卡车以10辆为一组前往车站。据博物院一位官员称，预计今日将有约5000箱珍宝运往南京。

这第二批货物是存于蒙塔班路本大楼和四川路32号的20,000箱中的一部分。在周三的第一批货物中，约有3351箱珍贵珍宝已运往南京。蒙塔班路本大楼内的珍宝将首先搬出，在随后的批次中，四川路本大楼内剩余的珍宝将被搬出。第三和第四批货物定于下周一和周四发运。

这批珍宝运抵首都后，将暂时存放在由一家外国公司建造的特制保险库中，直到为公众展示而永久安置的安排完成为止。该收藏包括91余箱艺术珍宝，这些珍宝曾于1935年11月至今年3月在伦敦伯灵顿府（Burlington House）展出。

REPORT

Date 30th June 1936.

Subject (in full) Transportation of Chinese Arts Treasures.

Made by D.S.I. Shields Forwarded by Insp. Edoova

Sir,

between 8.40 a.m. and 8.45 a.m. 30/6/36 seven motor lorries
laden with Chinese arts treasures (84 articles in all), passed
along North Honan Road from Soochow Road, Taipei to the Chinese
Arts Treasure Bureau, at the junction, French Concession.

Motor Lorries Lic. Nos. 16966, 16721, 16698, 17202, 17057,
17002 and 16964.

Mr. Wang Tuh Foo (汪德數), representative of the Chinese
Arts Treasure Bureau, accompanied the above lorries.

The party was escorted by the Reserve Unit.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,
J. J. Shields
D. S. I.

D.D.O. "C" Div.

Officer i/c.
Special Branch.
